2026-03-13.teaser: Today's collection spans the full spectrum of technological disruption and its real-world consequences. We've got breakthrough energy plays that could reshape manufacturing, shocking security breaches that expose the vulnerability of enterprise AI systems, and deep dives into how entire industries operate in regulatory gray zones. From Chinese AI companies building on open-source foundations to the shadowy economics of online gaming, these stories reveal the messy, complex reality behind the headlines. Each piece offers something you won't find in your typical tech coverage.

included.title: How We Hacked McKinsey's AI Platform
included.source: X/Twitter bookmark via Dr Efi Pylarinou
included.summary: A security research team at CodeWall.AI successfully breached McKinsey's enterprise AI platform, Lilly, using autonomous agents to access massive amounts of sensitive data without authentication. The hack exposed 46.5 million chat messages and revealed fundamental security vulnerabilities in enterprise AI systems that are increasingly trusted with confidential business information. The breach highlights a critical gap between the rapid deployment of AI platforms and the implementation of robust security measures. The autonomous nature of the attack demonstrates how AI tools can be weaponized against AI systems, creating new categories of cyber threats. The scale of accessible data suggests that many organizations may be unknowingly exposing sensitive information through poorly secured AI interfaces. This incident raises urgent questions about data governance, authentication protocols, and the security architecture of enterprise AI platforms that handle confidential business communications and strategic information.

included.title: The Shadow Economy of Online Gaming: How Money Moves Beyond the Screen
included.summary: An investigative report reveals how banks, payment processors, and aggregators collaborated to enable transactions for shadow gaming operators by disguising them as legitimate e-commerce merchants. The investigation exposes a sophisticated network where gaming companies that couldn't secure direct payment processing relationships were quietly onboarded through alternative channels, circumventing regulatory oversight and compliance requirements. This shadow payment ecosystem allowed potentially illegal or unregulated gaming operations to process billions in transactions while appearing as standard retail businesses to financial institutions. The report details how payment aggregators served as intermediaries, creating layers of obfuscation that made it difficult for banks to identify the true nature of the underlying businesses. The investigation raises serious questions about due diligence practices in the payments industry and the effectiveness of current regulatory frameworks in monitoring high-risk sectors. The findings have implications for anti-money laundering compliance, consumer protection, and the broader integrity of digital payment systems that increasingly power the global economy.

included.title: OpenClaw: China's AI Stack
included.summary: Zhipu's launch of AutoClaw represents the culmination of a remarkable trend where every major Chinese AI company has built products around a single open-source project, creating an ecosystem that includes Moonshot's KimiClaw, MiniMax's MaxClaw, Alibaba's CoPaw, ByteDance's ArkClaw, and Tencent's WorkBuddy. This convergence around one foundational technology demonstrates how open-source projects can become the backbone of an entire national AI strategy, creating both opportunities and dependencies. The market response was immediate, with Zhipu's stock jumping 13% on the announcement, indicating investor confidence in this approach to AI development. This phenomenon highlights the power of open-source in democratizing AI capabilities while raising questions about technological sovereignty and the concentration of innovation around specific platforms. The Chinese AI companies' collective embrace of this technology stack suggests a coordinated approach to building competitive AI products without reinventing fundamental infrastructure. This strategy could accelerate innovation by allowing companies to focus on application-layer differentiation while sharing underlying technological foundations, though it also creates potential single points of failure for the entire ecosystem.

included.title: Swift Solar Acquires Meyer Burger to Build Gigawatt-Scale Solar Factory
included.summary: Swift Solar's acquisition of Meyer Burger represents a strategic shift from component supplier to end-product manufacturer, embodying the principle that superior technology should be used to compete directly rather than simply sold to others. Joel Jean at Swift Solar is applying this philosophy to solar manufacturing, using their advanced perovskite tandem solar cell technology to build a gigawatt-scale factory capable of producing highly efficient solar panels. The deal gives Swift Solar access to Meyer Burger's established manufacturing infrastructure and expertise, allowing them to scale their innovative technology rapidly. This vertical integration strategy challenges the traditional model where technology companies license their innovations to manufacturers, instead betting that controlling the entire value chain will create sustainable competitive advantages. The gigawatt-scale ambition signals Swift Solar's intention to compete directly with established solar panel manufacturers while leveraging their technological edge in efficiency. This approach could accelerate the adoption of next-generation solar technology by removing the intermediary step of technology licensing and ensuring that the most advanced innovations reach the market quickly. The acquisition demonstrates how breakthrough energy technologies are increasingly being paired with aggressive scaling strategies.

included.title: ITR Forms AY 2025-26: More Disclosures, Details on HRA, Home Loan, TDS
included.summary: India's new ITR forms for Assessment Year 2025-26 introduce significant changes that expand disclosure requirements and modify filing procedures for taxpayers. The most substantial change raises the asset disclosure threshold from ₹50 lakh to ₹1 crore in income, requiring high earners to provide comprehensive details of all assets in Schedule AL. This change affects a smaller but wealthier segment of taxpayers while reducing compliance burden for middle-income earners. The forms now allow taxpayers with long-term capital gains below ₹1.25 lakh to use simplified ITR-1 or ITR-4 forms, streamlining the filing process for small investors. Enhanced requirements for HRA and deduction details provide tax authorities with more granular information about common tax-saving claims, potentially improving compliance monitoring. A crucial addition requires separate reporting of capital gains before and after July 23, 2024, corresponding to budget changes that likely affected tax rates or exemptions. These modifications reflect the tax authority's dual approach of simplifying procedures for smaller taxpayers while increasing scrutiny and disclosure requirements for high-income individuals. The changes demonstrate India's evolving tax administration strategy, balancing ease of compliance with improved revenue collection and taxpayer monitoring.

included.title: Sarvam: Open is not sovereign
included.summary: This analysis challenges the conventional wisdom that open-source AI models automatically confer technological sovereignty, using Sarvam as a case study to examine the complex relationship between openness and independence in AI development. The piece argues that while open-source models provide access to code and weights, true sovereignty requires control over the entire AI value chain, including data, compute infrastructure, talent, and the ability to modify and improve foundational models independently. The author contends that countries and companies relying heavily on open-source models from foreign entities may actually be increasing their technological dependence rather than achieving independence. The analysis explores how Sarvam's approach to building AI capabilities intersects with broader questions about national AI strategies and the trade-offs between leveraging global open-source resources and developing indigenous capabilities. The piece examines whether open-source AI creates a false sense of technological autonomy while potentially deepening dependencies on the ecosystems, tools, and platforms controlled by the original model creators. This perspective challenges policymakers and technologists to think more critically about what genuine AI sovereignty requires in an increasingly interconnected global technology landscape.

2026-03-15.teaser: Today's digest spans from global chokepoints to AI breakthroughs that are reshaping how we work. We explore how a 33-kilometer stretch of water controls the world's energy supply, dive into the latest AI agent wars between Perplexity and Claude, and discover how non-technical professionals are building sophisticated AI systems from scratch. Plus, we examine the mindset shifts that separate AI novices from power users, and get a behind-the-scenes look at building autonomous AI teams that actually deliver results.

included.title: The chokepoint that powers the global economy
included.summary: The Strait of Hormuz represents one of the world's most critical economic vulnerabilities—a 33-kilometer-wide passage that carries 20 million barrels of oil and a fifth of global LNG supply daily. This analysis reveals how recent military conflicts transformed a regional dispute into a global economic crisis, with over 200 vessels anchored outside the strait as insurers withdrew coverage. The piece effectively demonstrates how geographic chokepoints create systemic risks in our interconnected economy. While alternative pipeline routes exist, they can only handle 4.2 million barrels per day—barely a fifth of normal Hormuz traffic. The concentration of energy flows through this narrow waterway, with Saudi Arabia, Iraq, and UAE accounting for 13.1 million barrels daily, illustrates a fundamental design flaw in global supply chains. When logistics networks are disrupted, the oil doesn't disappear—it simply can't move, creating artificial scarcity that ripples through markets worldwide. This case study serves as a stark reminder that in our globalized world, the most mundane geographic features can become the most consequential economic battlegrounds.

included.title: Perplexity Computer vs Claude: Pick the Right AI Agent
included.summary: Perplexity Computer represents a significant evolution in AI tooling—not just another chatbot, but a project orchestration system that dynamically routes tasks across 19 frontier models. The analysis cuts through the hype to examine whether this $200/month tool justifies its premium over established alternatives like Claude's suite. The key insight is architectural: rather than betting on a single model, Perplexity positions itself as an aggregator layer, using Claude Opus for coding, Gemini for research, GPT-5.2 for long-context tasks, and specialized models for specific functions. This approach acknowledges that no single AI excels at everything—a pragmatic stance that could define the next phase of AI development. However, the real test isn't technical capability but workflow integration. For users answering simple questions, cheaper tools suffice. The value proposition emerges for complex, multi-step projects requiring coordination across Gmail, Slack, Notion, and GitHub. Early adopters report monthly costs of $500-1,500, suggesting this targets serious business users rather than casual experimenters. The piece effectively positions this as a choice between depth (Claude's focused excellence) versus breadth (Perplexity's orchestrated ecosystem).

included.title: The Full Tutorial: 6 AI Agents That Run a Company — How I Built Them From Scratch
included.summary: This tutorial demystifies AI agent development by walking through the creation of six autonomous agents that handle real business operations—from intelligence scanning to content creation and social media management. What sets this apart from typical AI content is its focus on practical implementation using standard web technologies rather than specialized AI frameworks. The author deliberately avoids OpenAI Assistants API, LangChain, and AutoGPT, instead building on Next.js, Supabase, and PostgreSQL—a decision that makes the system more maintainable and cost-effective at just $8 monthly plus LLM usage. The agents don't just execute tasks; they develop relationships, remember lessons learned, and evolve their communication styles based on experience. An agent with extensive tweet engagement naturally starts referencing engagement strategies in other contexts. The system includes 10-15 daily conversations between agents—standups, debates, mentoring sessions—creating an emergent organizational culture. The transparency element, featuring a pixel-art office frontend showing real-time operations, transforms what could be an abstract system into something tangible and observable. This approach suggests that effective AI systems aren't about the most advanced tools, but about thoughtful architecture that enables genuine autonomy and learning.

included.title: Starting AI Today? This Is Exactly What I'd Do
included.summary: This piece addresses the fundamental misconception that AI adoption requires technical expertise, using the compelling story of a 54-year-old political consultant who built sophisticated AI agents without coding. The central thesis challenges the replacement narrative: experienced professionals aren't being displaced by AI, but those who combine domain expertise with AI capabilities become formidable competitors. The author identifies four critical mistakes: treating AI like a search engine, waiting to 'learn properly,' assuming coding prerequisites, and focusing on tools rather than thinking frameworks. The breakthrough insight involves giving AI 'hands'—the ability to see your environment, take direct action, and self-correct errors. This isn't about learning programming languages but about using code editors as environments where AI can operate autonomously. The consultant's success story—producing a $75,000 political consulting proposal in three hours—demonstrates that the barrier isn't technical skill but conceptual understanding. The piece effectively reframes AI adoption from a technical challenge to a strategic advantage. Rather than fearing obsolescence, experienced professionals should recognize that their judgment, taste, and domain knowledge become more valuable when amplified by AI's execution speed. This perspective shift from replacement anxiety to capability enhancement represents a mature approach to AI integration.

included.title: Starting AI Today? This Is Exactly What I'd Do
included.summary: This comprehensive guide tackles the psychological and practical barriers preventing professionals from effectively adopting AI, using real success stories to illustrate transformative potential. The narrative centers on a 54-year-old political consultant who overcame replacement anxiety to build AI systems that compress months of work into hours. The author identifies a crucial pattern: most people use AI reactively—asking questions, copying answers, manually implementing solutions—rather than creating environments where AI can act autonomously. The key insight involves shifting from AI-as-search-engine to AI-as-colleague, capable of seeing your workspace, making direct changes, and self-correcting mistakes. This doesn't require programming skills but rather understanding how to create actionable environments using tools like code editors. The political consultant's achievement—producing a complete $75,000 consulting proposal in three hours—demonstrates that domain expertise combined with AI capabilities creates competitive advantages rather than replacement threats. The piece emphasizes mindset over methodology: experienced professionals possess irreplaceable judgment, taste, and client relationships that AI cannot replicate. However, when these human capabilities are amplified by AI's execution speed, the combination becomes more powerful than either element alone. This framework positions AI adoption as strategic enhancement rather than existential threat.

2026-03-16.teaser: Today we're diving deep into the infrastructure that's reshaping how we work with AI. From self-hosted assistants that break free from browser tabs to geopolitical investment walls getting strategic makeovers, the landscape is shifting fast. We're also exploring what separates true AI agents from glorified chatbots—and why that distinction matters more than you think. These aren't just technical updates; they're glimpses into how intelligent systems are becoming genuinely useful tools rather than novelty conversations.

included.title: OpenClaw Masterclass
included.summary: OpenClaw represents a fundamental shift in how we interact with AI—from visiting chatbots in browser tabs to having an assistant that lives where you already work. This self-hosted framework connects to WhatsApp, Telegram, Discord, and other platforms you use daily, making AI feel less like a separate task and more like an integrated workflow tool. What sets OpenClaw apart is its transparent, file-based memory system using plain Markdown documents that store the assistant's identity, rules, and accumulated knowledge. Unlike black-box AI services, everything is visible, editable, and portable on your local machine. The system includes a comprehensive toolkit for web search, browser automation, PDF processing, scheduling, and multi-channel coordination. This isn't just about answering questions—it's about doing actual work. OpenClaw transforms AI from a conversational interface into an action-oriented assistant that can handle both small daily tasks and complex automated workflows. The key insight is that effective AI assistance requires persistent context and memory, not just powerful language models. By making that memory transparent and user-controlled, OpenClaw offers a compelling alternative to cloud-based AI services for users who want both capability and control.

included.title: Trimming the Chinese Wall
included.summary: India's recent relaxation of Press Note 3—the sweeping 2020 restrictions on foreign investment from bordering countries—reveals the unintended consequences of broadly written policy responses to geopolitical tensions. Originally designed as a targeted measure against Chinese investment during COVID-19, the policy inadvertently created barriers for legitimate investments from other neighboring countries and complex ownership structures involving multiple jurisdictions. The government's immediate clarification that the easing 'was not meant for Chinese firms' highlights the political sensitivity around any perceived softening toward China, even as the practical reality demands more nuanced investment screening. This episode illustrates a common policy challenge: crisis-driven regulations often cast too wide a net, capturing unintended targets while potentially missing their actual objectives. The story underscores how geopolitical tensions can create economic policy rigidity that persists long after the initial crisis, requiring careful recalibration to balance security concerns with economic pragmatism. India's approach reflects the broader global trend of investment screening mechanisms that attempt to separate legitimate business activity from strategic threats, but the blunt instrument of blanket restrictions often proves inadequate for complex modern capital flows. The ongoing refinement of these policies will likely require more sophisticated frameworks that can distinguish between different types of foreign investment based on actual risk assessment rather than geographic origin alone.

included.title: We Went Live on Substack and Built a Research Agent Using Claude Code. Here's What I Learned.
included.summary: The distinction between AI chatbots and true AI agents lies not in the underlying technology, but in how context and memory are structured. Most people use AI like a chatbot—crafting detailed prompts each session, manually providing context about their business, audience, and requirements every single time. This approach works but places the cognitive burden entirely on the user to maintain and communicate context. A genuine AI agent, as demonstrated through this content research system built with Claude Code, operates differently by reading persistent context files that contain business information, competitor data, and operational parameters before executing any task. This pre-loaded context transforms the interaction from lengthy prompt engineering to simple task delegation. The research agent showcased can transform three hours of manual competitive analysis into a four-minute automated process costing under ten cents, but the real innovation isn't the speed or cost—it's the persistent awareness that eliminates repetitive context-setting. The system scrapes competitor content, analyzes SEO gaps, and delivers strategic recommendations because it already understands the business context, target audience, and competitive landscape. This architectural difference between stateless chatbot interactions and stateful agent operations represents a fundamental evolution in how AI systems can be designed to serve as genuine productivity tools rather than sophisticated question-answering interfaces. The key insight is that effective AI assistance requires embedded context and memory, not just powerful language processing capabilities.

2026-03-18.teaser: Today's digest cuts through the noise with insights that matter. We explore how AI is evolving from simple chatbots into sophisticated content systems that understand context and connections. The great spreadsheet debate heats up as code generation threatens to disrupt billion-user workflows. A Netflix co-founder reveals the psychology behind successful negotiations with just two powerful words. India's electricity grid undergoes a quiet revolution that could reshape how we all pay for power. And finally, why even the most brilliant products need world-class sales teams to reach their potential.

included.title: How a Skill Graph Can Turn AI Into Your Content Team
included.summary: The evolution from simple AI prompts to sophisticated skill graphs represents a fundamental shift in how we should think about AI assistance. Rather than treating AI like a one-off chatbot that responds to isolated requests, skill graphs create interconnected systems of knowledge that transform AI into a contextually aware content engine. This approach involves creating multiple small Markdown files—each containing specific instructions for brand voice, platform styles, audience profiles, or workflows—then linking them together so AI can navigate between relevant contexts dynamically. The power lies not in the individual files but in their connections, allowing AI to understand relationships between different aspects of content creation. When an AI system can reference your brand voice while adapting to LinkedIn's format and targeting your specific audience, it stops producing generic outputs and starts generating content that feels authentically yours. This systematic approach addresses the core weakness of most AI-generated content: lack of context. Instead of hoping a single massive prompt will capture all nuances, skill graphs create a knowledge architecture that grows more valuable over time, turning AI from a simple tool into a comprehensive content system that understands your unique requirements and constraints.

included.title: Will AI Kill Spreadsheets?
included.summary: Andrew Chen's provocative thesis that AI code generation will obsolete spreadsheets has ignited a fascinating debate about the future of business tools. His argument centers on a compelling premise: spreadsheets are essentially business logic trapped in an inadequate interface, lacking version control, testing, and modularity. With AI dramatically lowering the barrier to creating real software, the traditional advantage of spreadsheets—accessibility to non-technical users—may be eroding. The implications are staggering: with roughly one billion spreadsheet users worldwide, even a 10% migration to AI-generated applications could unleash an explosion of micro-software that transforms how businesses operate. However, the counterarguments are equally compelling. Critics point out that spreadsheets' grid-based visualization provides immediate, intuitive data comprehension that code cannot easily replicate. The collaborative, iterative nature of spreadsheet work—where multiple stakeholders can quickly modify and experiment with data—may prove more valuable than the technical superiority of proper software architecture. This debate reflects a broader tension in the AI era: will powerful new capabilities completely displace familiar tools, or will they enhance and coexist with existing workflows? The answer likely depends on whether AI can preserve the accessibility and immediacy that made spreadsheets ubiquitous while delivering the power and reliability of real software.

included.title: The Two Most Powerful Words in Any Negotiation
included.summary: Netflix co-founder Marc Randolph reveals a deceptively simple yet psychologically powerful negotiation technique through a Disney customer service story. When his friend expressed disappointment about sold-out fast passes, a Disney employee's response—printing three replacement passes—demonstrated the unique power of those two words: "I'm disappointed." Unlike aggressive demands or logical arguments that trigger defensive responses, expressing disappointment creates an entirely different dynamic. It avoids accusation while implying unmet expectations, positioning the other party as someone who can choose to make things right rather than someone who must defend their position. This approach transforms adversarial negotiations into collaborative problem-solving conversations. The psychological mechanism is elegant: disappointment signals a gap between expectation and reality without assigning blame, making the other person genuinely want to bridge that gap. Randolph illustrates this with a friend's successful salary negotiation, where expressing disappointment about an offer led to productive discussion rather than defensive pushback. The technique works because it's disarming—it starts conversations rather than arguments, and signals that the gap between offer and expectation is meaningful and worth addressing. In a world where most people approach negotiations with demands, explanations, or frustration, the quiet power of disappointment cuts through defensive barriers and appeals to our fundamental desire to exceed expectations rather than merely meet minimum requirements.

included.title: The new rules of paying for electricity
included.summary: India's electricity sector is undergoing a quiet revolution through proposed amendments to consumer rights rules that could fundamentally reshape how we pay for power. The most significant change involves time-of-use pricing, challenging the century-old assumption that electricity should cost the same regardless of when it's consumed. This shift reflects India's dramatically changing energy mix, where solar power floods the grid during daylight hours while demand peaks in the evening. The proposed rules would allow differential pricing based on consumption timing, potentially making electricity cheaper during solar-abundant afternoons and more expensive during high-demand evenings. This isn't just theoretical—it's already visible on the Indian Energy Exchange where real-time pricing fluctuates dramatically throughout the day. The implications extend beyond individual bills to the entire grid's efficiency and sustainability. Time-based pricing could incentivize consumers to shift energy-intensive activities to off-peak hours, reducing strain on the grid and maximizing renewable energy utilization. For large consumers initially, and eventually all users, this represents a fundamental shift from flat-rate billing to dynamic pricing that reflects actual supply and demand conditions. The changes also include provisions for improved consumer rights and service standards, but the pricing revolution stands out as the most transformative element that could influence everything from industrial operations to household routines.

included.title: Your product won't sell itself
included.summary: Jason Rosenthal challenges the dangerous myth that exceptional products sell themselves, particularly as crypto enters its enterprise adoption phase. This belief, common among technical founders, overlooks the reality that even revolutionary products require sophisticated go-to-market strategies to reach their potential. The shift toward enterprise crypto adoption makes world-class sales organizations not just helpful but essential for scaling beyond product-market fit. Rosenthal argues that building a sales team can be as exciting and metrics-driven as engineering, offering tangible, measurable results that directly translate to revenue growth. The key insight is treating sales with the same obsessive attention to detail that founders apply to product development—focusing on processes, metrics, and continuous optimization. His step-by-step approach begins with hiring the right sales leader, someone who can design the entire go-to-market playbook and establish the processes by which deals are won. This isn't about adding a few salespeople; it's about creating a systematic approach to revenue generation that can scale and compete effectively. The enterprise sales motion becomes particularly crucial in crypto, where complex products require education, trust-building, and sophisticated relationship management. For technical founders who may resist investing in sales, Rosenthal's message is clear: a world-class sales organization can unlock growth levels that even the most brilliant product alone cannot achieve.

2026-03-15.teaser: Sometimes the most extraordinary business empires emerge not from grand visions, but from relentless focus on fundamentals. Today we explore how obsessive attention to controllable variables can transform a humble root beer stand into a global hospitality giant. The story reveals why fighting against expansion might be the secret to sustainable growth, and how mastering downside risk can turn economic downturns into competitive advantages. It's a masterclass in building without blueprints, where success comes not from predicting the future, but from creating systems robust enough to thrive in any future. The lessons here apply far beyond hospitality—they're about the patient art of empire-building through disciplined execution.

included.title: [Outliers] J.W. Marriott: Building an Empire Without a Master Plan
included.summary: This fascinating deep dive into Bill Marriott's business philosophy reveals how the world's largest hotel empire emerged from counterintuitive principles. Starting with a nine-seat root beer stand in Washington, DC, Marriott's journey to hospitality dominance wasn't driven by grand strategic vision but by obsessive focus on controllable variables and downside risk management. The most striking aspect? He actively resisted entering the hotel business until age 55, preferring to master adjacent markets first—including pioneering the airline catering industry. Marriott's approach centered on isolating variables like location selection and refusing to depend on forces beyond his control. This disciplined methodology allowed his company to expand during the Great Depression while competitors collapsed. The episode illuminates how sustainable empire-building often requires fighting your own growth instincts, choosing depth over breadth, and building systems robust enough to thrive regardless of external conditions. Rather than betting on market predictions, Marriott created a machine optimized for serving people well—a deceptively simple goal that became the foundation for extraordinary scale. His story challenges conventional wisdom about entrepreneurial ambition, suggesting that the most enduring businesses emerge from patient, methodical execution rather than visionary leaps.

2026-03-17.teaser: From Wall Street's surprising bet on coliving to the hidden architecture of enterprise software, this week's digest cuts through the noise to reveal where real money and power are moving. We explore why Goldman Sachs just made a statement acquisition, how AI might finally liberate us from legacy software hell, and the privacy battles brewing in your pocket. Plus, discover the NotebookLM features that could transform how you work with information. These aren't just tech stories—they're signals of fundamental shifts in how we live, work, and build.

included.title: Why the World Still Runs on SAP
included.summary: This a16z analysis cuts to the heart of enterprise software's biggest paradox: why Fortune 500 companies remain shackled to systems they openly despise. SAP, ServiceNow, and Salesforce dominate not through superior user experience—quite the opposite—but because they've become the digital DNA of modern business operations. The piece reveals the staggering costs of escape: SAP migrations can consume $700 million, three years, and armies of consultants, often resulting in systems that barely function beyond generating static reports. The insight here isn't just about legacy software's stickiness, but about AI's potential to fundamentally reshape this dynamic. Rather than wholesale replacement, the authors argue for a more nuanced future where AI becomes the intelligent interface layer, making these systems programmable and accessible while preserving the critical business logic embedded within them. This represents a massive market opportunity—not in building new systems of record, but in creating the control plane that makes existing ones actually usable. The winners will be platforms that first reduce migration risk and timeline, then expand into daily operations as trusted automation layers.

included.title: Goldman Sachs Just Bought a Coliving Company
included.summary: Goldman Sachs' acquisition of Urban Campus marks a watershed moment for the coliving industry, signaling its evolution from experimental housing model to institutional asset class. This isn't venture capital or private equity dabbling—it's one of the world's most sophisticated financial institutions making a permanent capital allocation to coliving operations. The timing is particularly striking, occurring as The Collective, once Europe's coliving darling, collapsed after failing to find a buyer, highlighting the sector's brutal consolidation phase. Meanwhile, Barcelona's coliving surge—a 900% increase in five years—has triggered mass protests and regulatory backlash, illustrating the tension between housing innovation and affordability concerns. The Goldman move validates what industry insiders have long argued: coliving's economics work at scale when properly executed. Urban Campus brings real assets, proven operations, and a track record across European markets—exactly the kind of mature platform that justifies institutional investment. For operators, this acquisition represents both validation and a new competitive reality where institutional capital will increasingly dominate. The message is clear: coliving has crossed the threshold from alternative experiment to mainstream real estate strategy, with all the opportunities and challenges that institutional backing brings.

included.title: Do banking apps really need all these permissions?
included.summary: Zerodha's founder Nithin Kamath delivers a pointed critique of banking app privacy practices, highlighting a fundamental contradiction in financial technology security. While most banking apps demand extensive device permissions—access to SMS, contacts, phone functions—in the name of security, Kamath argues this violates the Principle of Least Privilege, a cornerstone of cybersecurity best practices. His company's approach offers a compelling counter-narrative: Zerodha's Kite app requests zero permissions on mobile devices, relying instead on SEBI's mandatory two-factor authentication framework to balance security with privacy. This isn't just a technical debate—it's a philosophical one about trust, user agency, and the true nature of digital security. Kamath's position challenges the industry's permission-heavy approach, suggesting that robust security can coexist with minimal data access. The broader implications extend beyond banking to any app that claims security justifies invasive permissions. His 'golden rule' philosophy—don't do unto others what you don't want done unto you—offers a refreshing alternative to the surveillance capitalism model that dominates fintech. For millions of users who've grown accustomed to surrendering digital privacy for financial services, Zerodha's approach demonstrates that this trade-off isn't inevitable.

included.title: 3 Hidden NotebookLM Features Most People Don't Use
included.summary: This deep dive into NotebookLM's ecosystem reveals how Google's research tool transforms when connected to its broader AI infrastructure. While most users treat NotebookLM as a standalone research assistant, the piece explores three powerful integrations that unlock entirely new capabilities: Gemini Canvas for visual collaboration, Gems for persistent AI personalities, and Antigravity for automated research workflows. The author's previous work connecting NotebookLM to Claude via MCP focused on external integrations, but this exploration maps the internal Google ecosystem connections that many users overlook. These aren't just feature additions—they represent a fundamental shift in how AI tools can work together within a unified platform. Gemini Canvas turns research into visual, collaborative workspaces. Gems create specialized AI assistants that maintain context and personality across sessions. Antigravity automates the research pipeline itself, creating systems that continuously gather and process information. The implications extend beyond productivity hacks to suggest a future where AI tools form interconnected workflows rather than isolated applications. For power users, these connections transform NotebookLM from a research tool into a comprehensive knowledge management and creation platform, demonstrating how platform integration can multiply individual tool capabilities exponentially.
